title: What? - Me Slow Down!
summary: A generation from now, energy scholars may search for clues on why, how and when American motorists' seemingly inalienable right to burn high-quality, cheap and plentiful gasoline eroded. Without the current emotional fog of blame-game antics obstructing their view, these researchers might wonder why the simple and effective fuel savings actions of driving slower or driving less or driving more efficient vehicles were not practiced more by today's drivers to relieve their burden of gasoline price. Rather than promoting proven conservation measures, US politicians seem inclined to take a whack at cutting gasoline price by re- crafting an anti-trust law.

children.summary: It is no secret that the ability of US refineries to fully satisfy domestic gasoline demand has long past. It is also well known that US imports of gasoline and blendstocks, mainly into the East Coast, have grown dramatically.

children.title: Europe Sails to the Rescue
children.summary: The 140 thousand bbls per day rise in imports between 2004 and 2006 represents the typical gasoline output of a 280 thousand barrel per day refinery. No new East Coast refineries, however, were built during this period.

children.title: Suing for Relief
children.summary: Lately the price pain to US motorists needed to entice extra gasoline-like stocks from foreign sources has become more and more burdensome. A form of relief from these gas pains has been touted as a price conspiracy suit against OPEC.
